english: Let $C$ be the parabola whose focus is the point $S(1,1)$ and whose directrix is the line $3x+4y+3=0$. Then the area of the region bounded by $C$ and the line $3x+4y=47$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ वह परवलय है जिसकी नाभि बिन्दु $S(1,1)$ है तथा जिसकी नियता रेखा $3x+4y+3=0$ है। तब $C$ तथा रेखा $3x+4y=47$ से परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: Distance of $S$ from the directrix $=\dfrac{|3+4+3|}{5}=2=2a\Rightarrow a=1$; vertex is at distance $1$ from the directrix

The line $3x+4y=47$ is parallel to the directrix (perpendicular to the axis) at distance $\dfrac{|47+3|}{5}=10$ from it, on the side of $S$ (since $3+4=7>-3$); so it is at distance $h=9$ from the vertex
In the parabola's own frame $Y^{2}=4X$ the line is $X=9$: chord $=2\sqrt{36}=12$
Archimedes: area of the segment $=\dfrac{2}{3}\times$ chord $\times h=\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot12\cdot9=72$
solution_full: The axis of $C$ is the line through $S$ perpendicular to the directrix $3x+4y+3=0$, i.e. along the direction $(3,4)$.

Distance of $S(1,1)$ from the directrix: $\dfrac{|3(1)+4(1)+3|}{\sqrt{9+16}}=\dfrac{10}{5}=2$. This distance is $2a$, so $a=1$; the latus rectum is $4a=4$ and the vertex lies on the axis at distance $a=1$ from the directrix.

The line $3x+4y=47$ is parallel to the directrix, so it is perpendicular to the axis. Its distance from the directrix is $\dfrac{|47-(-3)|}{5}=10$. The focus gives $3x+4y=7$, which lies between $-3$ and $47$, so the line is on the same side of the directrix as the focus, at distance $10-1=9$ from the vertex.
Distances are unchanged by a rotation and a translation, so in a frame with the vertex at the origin and the axis as the $X$-axis the parabola is $Y^{2}=4aX=4X$ and the line is $X=9$.
The line meets the parabola where $Y^{2}=36$, $Y=\pm6$: the chord has length $12$.

By Archimedes' result, the parabolic segment has area $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the rectangle on the chord with height $9$ (the tangent at the vertex is parallel to the chord): area $=\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot12\cdot9=72$.
originality_note: New: a tilted parabola given only by focus and directrix, cut by a line parallel to the directrix; the messy second-degree equation is never needed because the area depends only on two distances (way 4, hidden invariant). Closest known: area of the segment cut off by the latus rectum or a double ordinate of y^2 = 4ax. Different because: the student must read a and the chord's distance from the vertex from the focus-directrix data of a rotated parabola before Archimedes' 2/3 rule applies.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard parabola:: Focus-directrix distance gives 2a = 2, the vertex is midway, and the given line is recognised as perpendicular to the axis at distance 9 from the vertex.
concept_use.Area of a parabolic segment (Archimedes': The region is a parabolic segment; its area is 2/3 of chord x height = (2/3)(12)(9) by Archimedes' result.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that the line lies on the focus side of the directrix and meets C in two points, that the region bounded by C and the line is a single bounded region, and that 72 is a positive two-digit integer as planned (grid count 71.99). Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing that only distances matter: 2a from focus-directrix distance and the chord's distance 9 from the vertex, then Archimedes.
justification: Two linked ideas (reading the parabola's elements from a rotated focus-directrix description, and the 2/3 segment rule) in numerical format; a student who expands the second-degree equation faces heavy algebra. Between the routine area anchor 2024-P2-Q2 (L2) and the chord-area locus 2025-P2-Q6 (L4).
